summary: Tested NEW Yann AI Assistant backend integration (Claude Sonnet 4.5 via emergentintegrations). All 10/10 backend tests pass: GET /api/yann/quota (limit=30 returned correctly), POST /api/yann/chat (200 with French reply mentioning MesureChâssis context), follow-up in same session mentions prices 19,99€/59,99€/249€ from system prompt, empty message → 400, >2000 chars → 400, no-auth → 401, GET /api/yann/history works for own session and returns 403 cross-user. MongoDB persistence verified in yann_conversations + yann_quota counter increments. Step 11 (quota cap 31st message → 429) was SKIPPED as instructed to save LLM credits — code path inspection confirms logic is correct (check before increment, returns 429 with message). NOTE: prior backend logs showed a transient 502 with 'Budget has been exceeded! Current cost: 0.005463, Max budget: 0.001' from emergentintegrations/litellm — this did NOT repeat during my test run (all chat calls 200 OK), so it may be intermittent or model-specific budget metering. Worth monitoring.

minor.issue: Observed transient 502 with 'litellm.BadRequestError: Budget has been exceeded! Max budget: 0.001' in backend.err.log prior to my test run. Subsequent calls succeeded. May indicate EMERGENT_LLM_KEY has per-call budget that can fluctuate, OR model 'claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929' pricing on the budget side is misconfigured. Did not reproduce during 2 chat calls in my pytest run.

Validation order: Pydantic accepts {message: ''} and route raises HTTPException(400, 'Message vide'). Works correctly but error is plain text detail, not the structured {code,message} pattern used elsewhere (e.g. deps.py). Cosmetic only.

quota_remaining is computed as `max(0, 30 - used_today - 1)` BEFORE the increment is persisted — relies on `used_today` snapshot. Under concurrent calls the quota check is not atomic (read then $inc), so 2 racing requests at count=29 could both pass. Acceptable for MVP.

action_items: Monitor EMERGENT_LLM_KEY budget — the transient 'Max budget: 0.001' 502 should not recur but verify in production by checking backend.err.log periodically.
Consider making the quota check atomic via findOneAndUpdate with conditional $inc to avoid race-condition over-spend on the 30/day cap.
Optional: add server-side maximum of 30 chars on context_block reconstruction to keep prompts cheap (already capped at last 20 messages, good).
critical_code_review_comments: routes/yann.py is 235 lines — well under the 700-line threshold, single-purpose, clean.
Pydantic models present (ChatRequest, ChatResponse) — input validated.
MongoDB _id correctly NOT returned (only specific fields are returned in responses).
auth_user dependency reused — consistent with rest of codebase.
Cross-user session leak prevention is implemented in BOTH /chat and /history (good defense-in-depth).
EMERGENT_LLM_KEY loaded from env — no hardcoding.
System prompt teaches model the prices (19,99€/59,99€/249€) and they are correctly emitted in follow-up responses (validated by test_chat_followup_mentions_prices).
seed_data_creation: Only test_history_cross_user_forbidden inserts a temporary doc in yann_conversations (session_id=yann_otheruser_999999) and deletes it at the end of the test. No persistent test data left behind.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Yann routes are stable. Step 11 (quota cap = 30/day → 429) was deliberately skipped to save LLM credits, but code path is correct: line 125 of /app/backend/routes/yann.py checks `used_today >= DAILY_MESSAGE_LIMIT` and raises HTTPException(429). To validate cheaply, set `db.yann_quota.update_one({user_id, date: today_iso}, {$set:{count:30}}, upsert=True)` then POST /api/yann/chat — must return 429. test_yann.py is regression-ready.
